Alex's follow up to "Recursive Language Models" is out! 

"Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers"

This paper shows how an RLM can take on a task 64x longer than the ones it trained on. It learns how to split up the work on short examples, then reuses that strategy at up to 4 million tokens.

The authors also trained RLM-27B on synthetic tasks that simulate tool and sub-agent responses. Across 8 long-context benchmarks, it scored 26.9% higher on average than Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness, using about half as many tokens at inference.

Published exclusively on alphaXiv!

I bump into him later that day 

I say “well, was meant to be”

He says “oh hi” and walks away. 

The end.
